clue.text: Like the alliance consenting to ouija?

definitions.text: Like the alliance consenting to ouija?

parts.words: Like the alliance consenting to ouija?
parts.note: the word ouija is built from the French and German words for yes, so an alliance agreeing in both tongues fits

explanation.surface: A question about an alliance that agrees to use a spirit board.
explanation.walkthrough: Ouija joins OUI (French for yes) and JA (German for yes), so 'consenting to ouija' is saying yes in French and in German, as a partnership of those two nations would.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership of France and Germany is described by the hyphenated adjective naming both nations.

clue.text: Pigeon enthusiast on train

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or devotee
the train of a dress or a bird is its tail

explanation.surface: A pigeon fancier riding a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a breed of domestic pigeon with a fan-shaped spread of tail feathers.

clue.text: Laos revolution, moreover

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of the country's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uprising in the Southeast Asian country Laos, and what's more.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words add a further point to what has been said, meaning in addition or besides.

clue.text: Medical orderly bagged

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters of the word medical are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly caught or bagged something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medical orderly' reads as a hospital porter, but 'orderly' is the anagram signal working on MEDICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bagged something is to have taken it as your own, as when a prize or seat is staked out.

clue.text: He takes chances as a leisurely walker at Gateshead

indicators.note: Gateshead is in Tyneside, where the local burr makes the letter R sound throaty, so the walker's name is heard with a guttural start

parts.note: a rambler is someone who walks the countryside for pleasure

explanation.surface: A gambling man described as a stroller in a north-east English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town on the Tyne in north-east England; the Northumbrian burr pronounces R at the back of the throat, so the setter has RAMBLER said there come out like GAMBLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bets or risks money on uncertain outcomes is a person who takes chances.

clue.text: Salary increase, we hear, produces beams

indicators.note: says the pay rise is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: Getting a pay rise makes someone beam with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts of light from the sun are beams, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Unyielding first man with a New Testament following

indicators.note: says the scripture abbreviation comes after the other pieces

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man

explanation.surface: Biblical Adam stands firm, with the New Testament coming after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant refuses to be moved or persuaded, the same as being unbending.

clue.text: How Tennyson's brook went in strange, lively dance

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, matching the adverb answer

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made to dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet's stream moving in an odd, lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tennyson's poem 'The Brook' the refrain runs 'men may come and men may go, But I go on for ever'. 'dance' rearranges STRANGE plus LIVELY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The brook says it goes on for ever, so it flows endlessly, without stopping.

clue.text: Perhaps a sport certain to D be put off

indicators.note: signals that the following letters could perhaps be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture that is sure to be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges the thirteen letters of A SPORT CERTAIN; 'to be' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to delay or defer doing something, the sense of putting it off.

clue.text: Redgrave in the lead overseas

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army or movement, so to be in the van is to be in the lead

indicators.note: signals that the following short word is turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress taking the leading role abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Vanessa Redgrave is the English actress. 'over' acts on SEAS to give ESSA; the printed 'overseas' is read as two words, 'over seas'.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Redgrave's first name supplies the answer, a forename defined by its famous bearer.

clue.text: West End site of spring carnival?

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a fair is a carnival or funfair

explanation.surface: A fashionable London district that hosts a spring festival.
explanation.walkthrough: London's West End is its smart central district; Mayfair is one of its wealthiest areas, named after an annual fair held there in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayfair is an upmarket district in central London's West End.

clue.text: Buck up or bring up

explanation.surface: Two phrasal verbs offered as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that bucks up rises onto its hind legs, and to bring up a child is to raise it.

clue.text: This fish stank

explanation.surface: A fish that gave off a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small silvery fish, and smelt is also a British past tense of to smell, meaning gave off an odour.

clue.text: Mineral found in hospital cupboards

indicators.note: says the answer is tucked inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A mineral powder kept in hospital storage cupboards.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, magnesium silicate, ground into powder.

clue.text: Care needed after start of Sandown-it is the turf

indicators.note: says the care piece follows the opening letter
the opening letter of the racecourse name is taken

parts.note: to be in ward is to be in someone's care or keeping

explanation.surface: A racecourse's grass needing attention, as at Sandown Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandown Park is an English racecourse; 'it is the' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is an expanse of short grass, the same as turf.

clue.text: In the east Iraqi troops are on the move

indicators.note: says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Iraqi troops in the east are moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, active and in motion.

clue.text: Permitted everybody with ring to get married

parts.note: all means everybody
O is ring-shaped
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Everyone with a wedding ring was allowed to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted and allowed both mean given leave or authority to do something.

clue.text: Stone tablet provides an Egyptian quay, we hear

definitions.text: Stone tablet provides an Egyptian quay, we hear

parts.words: Stone tablet provides an Egyptian quay, we hear
parts.note: quay is said like key: a carved stone that gave the key to Egyptian writing

explanation.surface: An inscribed stone describing a wharf on the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rosetta Stone, found at a port in the Nile delta, carried one text in three scripts and so gave scholars the key to hieroglyphs; 'quay' sounds like that key.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous inscribed slab from Egypt that unlocked hieroglyphic script is named after the town where it was found.

clue.text: Possibly the near eastern capital

indicators.note: says the following letters could possibly be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Older spelling of Tehran, the Iranian capital. 'Possibly' rearranges THE NEAR; the surface wants 'near eastern capital' as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran, spelt here in its older form, is the capital city of Iran, in the East.

clue.text: Was upset after kick on shin I cut up rough!

indicators.note: says the upturned word follows the kick

parts.note: in football and rugby a hack is a kick on the shins

indicators.note: set upside down, so in this down clue the word was is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone upset after being kicked on the shin makes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns WAS to SAW, which follows HACK. The definition speaks as the tool: a hacksaw cuts roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, and a tool speaking for itself could claim to cut things roughly.

clue.text: Arrived at last at an insignificant place

explanation.surface: Someone finally turns up in an unimportant spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'now here' the answer means arrived at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it says someone has come at last; as one word it names an obscure spot, as in the middle of nowhere.

clue.text: Wager about chance of getting meat

indicators.note: says the wager goes around the chance

parts.note: a bet is a wager
a risk is a chance of loss

explanation.surface: Placing a bet on the chance of winning a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, a type of meat.

clue.text: Bar fuse being blown, it can be conducted away

indicators.note: a blown fuse breaks, so the letters of those words are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: An electrical fuse blowing in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being blown' rearranges BAR FUSE. A bus conductor took the money from passengers, so the fare is conducted away.
explanation.definitionFit: The money collected by a bus conductor from a passenger is the ticket price.

clue.text: Common nappers are nearly always cured

definitions.text: Common nappers are nearly always cured

parts.words: Common nappers are nearly always cured
parts.note: people who kip are sleepers, and the smoked herrings of the same name are nearly always cured

explanation.surface: Ordinary people who doze can usually be healed.
explanation.walkthrough: To kip is British slang for to sleep, so those who kip are nappers; the same word names smoked herrings, which are cured fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoked split herrings sold for breakfast share their name with people who sleep.

clue.text: Pleasant resort

explanation.surface: A pleasant holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice means pleasant, and Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Oliver's tobacco?

explanation.surface: A question about a man named Oliver's smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan; twist is also tobacco rolled into a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan hero has this surname, and tobacco twisted into a thick cord is also known by it.

clue.text: Short drive-second to flag

parts.note: on a golf green the pin is the flagstick

explanation.surface: A golfer's short drive coming second to the flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short drive' suggests golf, as does 'flag', but the definition is a brief ride in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure trip in a car.

clue.text: Borodin's prince — soldier st turning yellow

indicators.note: says the soldier's letters are turned round

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A Russian opera prince as a soldier turning cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Borodin wrote the opera 'Prince Igor'. 'turning' reverses GI to IG.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Borodin's opera is the medieval Russian prince of that name.

clue.text: Flightless bird yet seen on the wing at Twickenham

definitions.text: yet seen on the wing at Twickenham

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly is nonetheless seen flying at a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is England's national rugby ground; New Zealanders are nicknamed after their national bird, and a New Zealand player may play on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is New Zealand's flightless national bird, and a New Zealander is nicknamed after it.

clue.text: Pasta as angel-surprise

indicators.note: a surprise shakes things up, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pasta served as a heavenly surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a type of pasta in wide flat sheets.

clue.text: Insect going round tree can be taken as food

indicators.note: says the insect surrounds the tree

parts.note: an ant is an insect
the lime is a tree

explanation.surface: An insect circling a tree that can be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be taken as' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Opposing factions under oath?

parts.note: groups who have pledged themselves to oppose each other, with sworn read as under oath

explanation.surface: A question about rival sides who have taken a solemn vow.
explanation.definitionFit: Implacable foes who have vowed hostility are described by this phrase.
